title: Structure of the atom and quantum physics
summary: The nuclear model from alpha scattering, nuclear notation, photons and atomic spectra, energy levels, and (HL) the Bohr model, nuclear radius, the photoelectric effect, matter waves and Compton scattering.

keyterms.definition: An atom has a tiny, dense, positive nucleus containing almost all its mass, surrounded mostly by empty space with electrons.
Alpha particles fired at thin gold foil; rare large-angle deflections revealed a small massive nucleus.
A: the total number of protons and neutrons in a nucleus.
Z: the number of protons in a nucleus, which identifies the element.
A quantum of electromagnetic energy, E = hf = hc/λ.
One of the discrete energies an electron in an atom may have.
Bright lines at specific wavelengths emitted when electrons drop between energy levels.
Dark lines in a continuous spectrum where atoms absorb photons that match level differences.
Hydrogen model with quantized angular momentum mvr = nh/2π and levels E = −13.6/n² eV.
Emission of electrons from a metal surface when light above a threshold frequency falls on it: E_max = hf − Φ.
Minimum energy Φ needed to remove an electron from a metal surface.
Wavelength associated with a moving particle: λ = h/p.
Increase in wavelength of an X-ray photon scattered by an electron: Δλ = (h/m_ec)(1 − cos θ).

questions.prompt: In the Geiger–Marsden experiment, what did the very rare large-angle deflections of alpha particles show?
options: Positive charge and most mass are concentrated in a tiny nucleus
questions.explanation: Only a tiny, massive, positive nucleus could repel alphas strongly enough to turn them back. Most passing straight through showed the atom is mostly empty.

questions.statement: Most alpha particles passed straight through the gold foil with little or no deflection.
questions.explanation: This showed that most of the atom is empty space.

questions.text: A nucleus of uranium-238 (Z = 92) contains ___ neutrons.
questions.explanation: Neutrons = A − Z = 238 − 92 = 146.

questions.prompt: Match each symbol or term to its meaning.
questions.explanation: Nuclide notation writes A above and Z below the element symbol.

questions.prompt: Why was gold foil used in the scattering experiment?
options: It can be made extremely thin and has heavy nuclei
questions.explanation: Very thin foil means each alpha meets few nuclei; large Z gives strong repulsion.

questions.prompt: The radius of an atom is roughly how many times larger than the radius of its nucleus?
questions.explanation: Atoms are about 10⁻¹⁰ m across; nuclei about 10⁻¹⁵ m, a factor of about 10⁵.

questions.statement: Electrons in the nuclear model are found inside the nucleus.
questions.explanation: The nucleus holds protons and neutrons; electrons occupy the surrounding space.

questions.text: In the Geiger–Marsden experiment, the force that deflected alpha particles was the electrostatic (___) force.
questions.explanation: Repulsion between the positive alpha and the positive nucleus, F = kq₁q₂/r².

questions.prompt: Which nucleus has 8 protons and 10 neutrons?
Order the development of atomic models.
questions.explanation: Each model was replaced when experiments revealed something it could not explain.

questions.text: A photon of wavelength 500 nm has energy ___ × 10⁻¹⁹ J (h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹).

questions.prompt: An electron drops from a level at −1.5 eV to one at −3.4 eV. The emitted photon has energy

questions.statement: Line spectra are evidence that electrons in atoms have only discrete energies.
questions.explanation: Only specific photon energies appear, matching differences between fixed energy levels.

questions.prompt: Dark lines in the spectrum of starlight are caused by
options: absorption by cooler gas in the star’s outer layers
questions.explanation: Atoms in the cooler atmosphere absorb photons that match their level differences, removing those wavelengths.

questions.prompt: Match each spectrum type to its appearance.

pairs.right: Bright lines on a dark background
Dark lines on a continuous spectrum

questions.explanation: Comparing line positions identifies the elements present.

questions.text: An atom with four energy levels can emit up to ___ different photon energies.
questions.explanation: The number of possible transitions between 4 levels is 4 × 3/2 = 6.

questions.prompt: Which photon has the greatest energy?
questions.explanation: E = hf, so the highest-frequency photon (ultraviolet here) has the most energy.

questions.statement: An atom can absorb a photon of any energy greater than the gap between two levels and keep the excess.
questions.explanation: For bound–bound transitions the photon energy must match the level difference exactly.

questions.prompt: The emission and absorption lines of the same element occur at
questions.explanation: Both involve the same energy-level differences.

questions.prompt: Order the processes producing an emission line.
items: Electron moves to a higher level
Electron falls back to a lower level
Photon with energy ΔE is emitted
questions.explanation: The photon’s energy equals the difference between the two levels.

questions.text: In the Bohr model, the energy of the n = 2 level of hydrogen is ___ eV.

questions.prompt: Light of frequency above the threshold frequency falls on a metal. Increasing the intensity
options: increases the maximum kinetic energy of electrons
increases the number of electrons emitted per second
questions.explanation: Higher intensity means more photons per second, so more electrons; each photon’s energy hf is unchanged, so E_max is unchanged.

questions.prompt: Photons of energy 4.0 eV hit a metal with work function 2.5 eV. The maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons is

questions.statement: Below the threshold frequency, very bright light will eventually release photoelectrons.
questions.explanation: Each photon must individually supply at least Φ; the wave model wrongly predicted energy could build up.

questions.text: An electron (m = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg) moving at 1.0 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹ has de Broglie wavelength ___ nm (h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s).

questions.prompt: Which experiment showed that electrons have wave properties?
questions.explanation: Electrons diffract with λ = h/p, comparable to atomic spacing.

questions.prompt: Match each experiment to what it shows.
questions.explanation: Each experiment supports a key quantum idea.

questions.prompt: In Compton scattering, the wavelength shift is greatest when the photon is scattered through
questions.explanation: Δλ = (h/m_ec)(1 − cos θ) is largest when cos θ = −1, i.e. θ = 180°.

questions.prompt: The radius of a nucleus is R = R₀A^(1/3). How does the nuclear density depend on A?
options: It is roughly independent of A
questions.explanation: Volume ∝ R³ ∝ A and mass ∝ A, so density is about the same for all nuclei.

questions.prompt: A graph of E_max against frequency for photoemission is a straight line. Its gradient is
questions.explanation: E_max = hf − Φ: gradient h, x-intercept the threshold frequency, y-intercept −Φ.
